finding: the five distribution copies of the nanomem package are four releases stale and untracked in git
git: all five live under untracked trees ('Launch 1/', 'nanomem_mac_bundle/'), so no commit in this project has ever updated them
drift: 12-13 files differ per copy against HEAD's nanomem_standalone/nanomem
what_the_stale_bundles_still_contain: engine 3.0.3 reads temporal_direction's default as an INSTRUCTION, so 'what was my original address?' is answered with the CURRENT value (9.0% top-1 on historical questions vs a plain cosine scan's 22.0%) -- fixed in 3.0.4
the pre-3.0.5 arena allocation: a 71,433-document load peaks at ~818 MB ru_maxrss instead of ~286 MB
no arena sidecar and no PCA screen (3.1.0), so reopen is the slow path
WriteClassifier threshold 0.60, which drops about 32% of answerable facts; 0.05 is worth +13.3 pt end-to-end (0.5.0)
wheels: every .whl in the tree is nanomem-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl; nanomem/__init__.py already carries a standing NOTE FOR WHOEVER PUBLISHES that it must be rebuilt
why_not_fixed_in_this_commit: Syncing five bundles across four releases changes user-visible defaults (a new .arena file appears beside every vault, the write gate keeps ~57% more turns, top-10 lists can reorder on ties) and would make a feature commit unreviewable. It is a distribution decision, not part of adding temporal primitives, and it should be its own commit with its own check that each bundle still runs.
recommended_next_step: one sync commit that copies nanomem_standalone/nanomem into the five copies, rebuilds the wheel from the current source, and puts the bundles under git so the drift cannot recur silently
